prize_parts.citation: For the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, in which atoms held at a magic wavelength allow optical frequency standards at the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: After the full first round my preferred configuration is unchanged: B041, Katori and Ye, as a single part. The original idea is the magic-wavelength lattice, which cancels the trap light shift while keeping Lamb-Dicke confinement, and the original experiments turned it into an instrument that interrogates very many neutral atoms at once. That is the kind of tool that opens a door, and the door has been walked through: Sr, Yb and Hg clocks in several countries compare at the 1e-18 level, so the result is verified in the way the statutes and my own experience ask for. The chair asked what it has taught us about nature. The honest answer is that it has measured gravitational redshift over millimetre height differences and set bounds on drifts of constants and on dark-matter couplings, without yet finding a deviation. I do not think a null result disqualifies it, since the capability is itself what the experiments verified, but I would keep the citation on the invention and the demonstrated accuracy and not promise discoveries that have not been made. The credit is the cleanest on the shortlist at two names, and I can say that I am sure of those two as the people who did the original work in concept and in record performance, subject to the historical check below.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection remains framing: a sceptic can call this a superb refinement of precision measurement and not a discovery that changes our picture of nature, and so far every test of fundamental physics with these clocks has been consistent with known physics. Overlap with the 2005 prize (combs) and the 2012 prize (control of single quantum systems) is the second objection, and I think it is answerable but not trivially. Third, the priority record is not fully checked by any of us. Several groups realised early strontium lattice clocks and early evaluations near 1e-17 to 1e-18, and PTB, SYRTE and NIST made real contributions. Fourth, support is broad but shallow, with three members placing it seventh in the opening round, and the redefinition of the second is still pending. B032 has the stronger conceptual claim for those who weigh a new organising principle most, and I take that seriously; my objection to it is about attribution, not science.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked B041 seventh partly because the redefinition of the second is pending, and supports B032 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp while accepting that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are missing.
responses.response: I have thought again about the pending redefinition and I still do not see it as a maturity condition for the physics. The redefinition is a decision of the metrology community that depends on comparison campaigns and on the choice of species, and it would not change what has been demonstrated in the laboratories. If the objection is overlap, I will answer that directly: the comb was the ruler and the ion prize was single-particle control, whereas the lattice clock is a separate invention for neutral ensembles. I agree with your own point on B032 that the theory-experiment chain is incomplete whichever trio is chosen, and I would add that this is a procedural problem for the committee and not a scientific weakness of the topological insulator. If you can tell me what would make you move B041 above seventh, a scientific reason rather than a timing one, I would like to hear it.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers B032 with Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, covering theory, the 2D experiment and the 3D ARPES discovery, and says he could live with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp if the committee decides explicitly.
responses.response: I agree with you that the committee should decide the Mele question explicitly and not by default, and I appreciate your willingness to accept the three-name version without Hasan. My difficulty is with Hasan's name. Whether the first 3D observation by ARPES belongs to him against other ARPES groups is a matter of the historical record that neither of us has verified, and I cannot be absolutely sure that Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan identifies the people who did the original work. A citation tied to the 2D quantum spin Hall state would avoid the 3D problem, but then the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal that guided the HgTe experiment becomes the open question. I would rather not vote for a configuration whose credit I would have to defend on memory. On your point about a non-deviation: I accept it, and it is why my citation does not claim a discovery beyond the invention and its verified performance.

responses.point: Lindroth wants the B041 citation to say what is learned about nature and has left room for a third lattice-clock name.
responses.response: I agree with you on the citation, but only up to a point. A citation can say that the lattice clock enables tests of the gravitational redshift at millimetre scale and searches for varying constants, as capabilities that have been used, and it should not suggest more than that. I still hold at two names. The record is clear on Katori for the concept and Ye for bringing the many-atom platform to its present performance, and a third name from PTB, SYRTE or Takamoto's work would require an original experiment that the record shows to be earlier or decisive, which none of us has demonstrated. If a verified chronology showed that, I would reconsider, and I would want the committee to ask the Academy's experts for it before the citation is final. Your point that the prize is not a list of every important contributor is the one I would put in the committee's record.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B032 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp for its verified discovery of a new state of matter, and says B041 or B046 are cleaner if the attribution chain proves too contested.
responses.response: Your own fallback is revealing: you say B041 is cleaner if the attribution chain is too contested, and I think the chain is contested enough that none of us can resolve it from memory. I share your trust in the agreement between measured spectra and first-principles calculations, and the clock case rests on the same kind of agreement between independent laboratories and between experiment and the atomic-structure calculations of systematic shifts. I want to be fair to your case: conceptually B032 is the larger discovery, and if the committee verifies the priority between Kane-Mele and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and finds that three names fit, I would not oppose it. On the question the chair put, attribution cleanliness against conceptual novelty, I weigh cleanliness more, because the statutes require us to be sure who did the original work.

responses.point: Johansson prefers B031, circuit QED, as a new regime of strong single-photon coupling, discloses proximity to the field, and lists B041 as his first alternative.
responses.response: Thank you for the disclosure. For my part I do not think it calls for recusal, since you have said so openly and have named B041 as your first alternative, so the committee can simply weigh your ranking with that in mind. On the science, I do not question that strong coupling in a circuit is a real new regime. My concern is the one you raise yourself, that it follows so soon after the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, and that the credit among Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf leaves out Girvin and Huang and the shared Yale and ETH work. I would like to know whether you would accept B041 as a fallback because of the clean credit, or because of the science.

uncertainties: The dates and attribution for the first strontium lattice-clock operation and the first evaluations near 1e-17 and 1e-18 have not been checked against the record by anyone on the committee; a third name would be justified only if that record shows an earlier or decisive original experiment.
Whether the committee will see the lattice clock as a distinct invention from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and whether the three members who ranked it seventh object on scientific or on overlap grounds.
Whether the redefinition of the second, which is a metrological decision, is treated by others as a maturity condition. I do not, but the clock quantities I quote are from memory.

B032 may be the better prize if the Kane-Mele and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang priority and the 3D ARPES chronology can be verified so that three names are defensible; I have not been able to establish this.
B046 remains premature for me while the mechanism of superconductivity in magic-angle graphene is unsettled.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B041 from my profile, and I have no link to Katori or Ye. My field is electron microscopy, far from atomic clocks. Göran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague and Bernhard Mehlig works in the neighbouring Gothenburg department, with no collaboration with either on the shortlisted topics. Johansson's disclosure on B031 does not call for recusal in my view, only for the committee to weigh his ranking accordingly. No change to my earlier disclosure.
